ruling.recommended_action: Send the 10:04–10:11 segment to a human reviewer to determine whether the driven route matched the rider-agreed Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1; hold the $23.18 fixed quote unchanged unless the reviewer finds the segment was not on the agreed road (in which case record an RD-1 breach — no refund arises on a fixed RydeX fare).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a fixed-quote RydeX booking, and the fare record shows the billed distance (9.84 km) against the 9.8 km optimal route with no surge and no post-trip add-on, totalling $23.18 [F4][F5][F6]. Under RD-2 the non-metered branch refunds only ERP/toll actually incurred and unpublished add-ons, and the detour mileage does not enter a fixed quote at all, so the 2.21 km segment adds no refundable amount — there is no arithmetic to run because the fare record carries no per-km rate for this service [F3][F6][RD-2]. FARE-1 is also not engaged: the charged total is base + distance + time + platform only, all published components, and any unpublished item would have to be refunded — none is present [F6][FARE-1].

One off-route segment exists (10:04–10:11, 3.98 km where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, +2.21 km) [F3]. RD-4 gives it no cover: no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window, and a speed band alone is corroborative only [F11][F14][RD-4]. So the only possible excuse is the rider's agreement, and the parties agree the ground is a named-road agreement (both briefs file F3 as named_road_untied under RD-5/G13).

On that ground the record does not settle the case. The driver asked before the segment, at 10:01, to "go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1", and the rider's own message at 10:01 answered "Sure, no problem." — a rider message sent before the 10:04 segment start, so timing is satisfied [F7][F8][F3][F9][RD-5]. But a specific named road ("go round via X") covers driving on X only, and the record must tie the segment to X; nothing in the gps, fare or traffic facts names Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 or otherwise places the car on it, and timing alone is not a tie — G13 directs undetermined, not exempt [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. Nor does the driver's post-trip statement cure the gap: a claim of agreement in the driver's statement is not consent, and it names no road in a system record [F10][RD-5].

That undetermined finding must be read against the trace. The segment has been measured (✓ RD-1) and the RD-4 incident screen has failed (✗), but the RD-5 scope question is a "?" and, on a fixed fare with no prior upheld dispute, it changes neither the amount nor the flag — so the case could be closed; the record nonetheless cannot answer whether a rider-agreed route was actually driven, and the §6 gaps (G12/G13) direct such an unsettled reading tied to a driver's own route choice to a person. I therefore send it to a reviewer rather than filing it away [F3][F7][F8][RD-1][RD-5].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in the last 90 days, so the "repeated" precondition is absent for him as well as for the rider [F16][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: the chat is two messages — a traffic question and a one-line assent — the driver's statement recounts the same exchange, and the complaint is about route and fare [F7][F8][F10]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the messages, statement or complaint; safety_concern is "none" [SAFE-1].
